question: Atticoantral CSOM is considered the 'unsafe' type because the posterosuperior retraction pocket or pars flaccida perforation may harbour a cholesteatoma, making surgical clearance — not prolonged topical antibiotic therapy — the definitive treatment.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true and represents one of the most important clinical distinctions in ENT. Atticoantral CSOM (cholesteatoma ear) is inherently unsafe due to progressive bone erosion and the risk of intracranial extension. Surgery is mandatory; prolonged use of topical antibiotic drops is dangerous as it masks deterioration.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Atticoantral disease (unsafe CSOM) is associated with cholesteatoma, which destroys bone and risks intracranial complications. The definitive treatment is mastoid surgery (tympanomastoidectomy), not continued topical drops. Treating it medically is the most dangerous error in CSOM management.
